expectations.text: The registration-led promotion condition is engaged against the prompt's detail: the audience attends on employer training budgets, so registration-led is promoted or seriously weighed rather than dismissed
expectations.evidence: The 'What settles it for us' section links employer-paid training tickets to the skill's condition for promoting registration-led above the sponsor-led default. It splits the condition into two parts (employer budgets ✅, program clears budgets ❓) and explains why registration-led matters: its revenue scales with what the audience pays. It also names the costs. The decision then hinges on one question: yes → registration-led, no → sponsor-led for now. The header names it 'registration-led candidate'.

expectations.evidence: The transcript names the employer-training-budget detail outright: 'Your tickets are the strong revenue line. Employer-paid training budgets are less price-sensitive than individual or community buyers. That favors a ticket-led model.' It then builds a ticket-led rule on that basis, with tickets covering the fixed base and sponsors funding extras. It also compares this with Director B's conclusion and gives a sponsor-share range of 20–40%.
